## Sep 24 Recap: Finding the Strike Zone

From a pitcher's perspective, going 7-5 is like having your fastball working but leaving a few hangers over the plate. We commanded the zone on 58.3% of our calls yesterday, and that's the kind of consistency that wins ballgames over a long season. Let's break down what worked and where we missed our spots.

## The Wins That Landed

Seven picks hit their target yesterday, and most of them were no-doubters. The Diamondbacks and Cubs calls at 61% confidence were like painting the corners—those are the pitches you throw with conviction. The Yankees pick at 58% had good movement on it too. Even the tight ones like Rangers at 50% and Astros at 52% found their way across the plate. That's what I call working the edges of the zone.

## The Misses: Tipping Pitches?

Three losses stings a bit, especially that Braves call at 61% confidence. Sometimes even your best stuff gets hit. The Phillies miss at 57% and White Sox at 53% were borderline—those games could've gone either way. That's baseball. You learn, you adjust your grip, and you come back stronger the next day.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Red Sox Over Cubs

Let me tell you about Sep 25's best opportunity. We're looking at Clay Holmes taking the hill for the Cubs against Boston's Alec Gamboa at Fenway. The model likes the Red Sox at 57% confidence, and from a pitcher's perspective, I see why.

## The Pitcher's Take on This Matchup

Clay Holmes is transitioning from the bullpen world, and starting requires a different arsenal management. You can't just air it out for one inning—you need to pace yourself, work through the lineup multiple times. Alec Gamboa gets the home cooking at Fenway, and that familiarity with your park's dimensions matters more than people think.

The Red Sox at 57% isn't a slam dunk, but it's a quality pitch with good location. This is the kind of call where the home team edge and pitching matchup alignment give you that extra conviction. Trust your stuff and throw it.

**Tomorrow's game time will tell if we can build on today's 7-5 performance. Keep your mechanics sound and stay aggressive in the zone.**
